links.outcome: Model performance degradation from data drift during COVID pandemic
links.effect: Mean AUROC fell from 0.92 to 0.87 (-5.5%) and AUPR from 0.22 to 0.07 (-69.11%) on in-pandemic test data; input distributions differed significantly (Kolmogorov-Smirnov).
links.quote: The models produced showed excellent areas under receiver-operating characteristic and acceptable precision-recall curves when tested on a dataset from January-March 2020, but significant degradation when tested on a dataset collected in the first wave of the COVID pandemic from April-May 2020.

links.outcome: Performance of trained models on new-period data after sudden external change
links.effect: All model families deteriorated in-pandemic; none of the weighting, recent-data, or scaling modifications prevented the loss in performance.
links.quote: None of the modifications carried out could prevent the significant deterioration in performance.

unlisted_practices: Training-time robustness measures (time-weighting older data, using only recent data, z-scaling inputs) to prevent drift degradation

links.outcome: Temporal test performance under pandemic shift
links.effect: All native models: AUROC 0.92 (0.03) pre vs 0.87 (0.04) in-pandemic; AUPR 0.22 (0.05) vs 0.07 (0.02); p<0.001.
links.quote: The models produced showed excellent areas under receiver-operating characteristic and acceptable precision-recall curves when tested on a dataset from January-March 2020, but significant degradation when tested on a dataset collected in the first wave of the COVID pandemic from April-May 2020.

links.effect: Native all-model mean AUROC/AUPR fell 0.92/0.22 to 0.87/0.07 (p<0.001); modified models also lost performance.
links.quote: Most models suffer from a performance loss in the pandemic, not only the native ones, but also those modified by means of the “weight”, “6 months” and “scaled” methods.

links.outcome: Input distribution shift from development data
links.effect: Validation vs in-pandemic: age 56 vs 58, RPC ordered 27.0% vs 37.7%, consults 2.00 vs 3.00; all p<0.001; mortality p=0.458.
links.quote: During the pandemic, there was a change in the probability distribution of input features.

links.outcome: Performance degradation from concept and covariate drift
links.quote: Both the parametric and non-parametric methods represented in the AutoML framework experienced a loss of performance at the beginning of the COVID-pandemic which was caused by concept drift and covariate shift.

unlisted_practices: Preemptively weighting older training data less to improve robustness to sudden drift
Training only on the most recent six months of data to improve robustness to sudden drift
Z-transforming numerical inputs to improve robustness to covariate shift

links.outcome: AUROC and AUPR degradation under pandemic data drift
links.effect: Across 269 models, mean AUROC decreased from 0.92 to 0.87 (-5.50%) and mean AUPR decreased from 0.22 to 0.07 (-69.11%, both p < 0.001) during the COVID-19 pandemic.
links.quote: The models produced showed excellent areas under receiver-operating characteristic and acceptable precision-recall curves when tested on a dataset from January-March 2020, but significant degradation when tested on a dataset collected in the first wave of the COVID pandemic from April-May 2020.

unlisted_practices: Temporal sample weighting (weighting older training data weaker) during model training to prevent drift-induced performance degradation
Restricting model training data to the most recent historical period (e.g., past 6 months) to mitigate data drift
Z-score normalization of numerical input parameters to improve model robustness to sudden covariate shift

screen.practice: drift mitigation in model training (data weighting, recent-data training, z-transformation)
screen.reason: Empirically tests methods to mitigate model degradation from pandemic-induced data drift on surgical mortality risk prediction models.

primary.practice: training-time drift mitigation methods (temporal weighting, recency filtering, normalization)
